source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: The Sun and Mercury are deemed of common influence, and productive either of good or evil in unison with whatever planets they may be connected with.

condition.modulation: good or evil according to connected planets

normalized_rule: Classify the Sun and Mercury as common influence, productive of good or evil according to the planets with which they are connected.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific relational classification, not a guaranteed good or evil outcome.
review_notes: Keep common influence separate from fixed benefic/malefic categories; the source explicitly makes its result depend on connections.
source_terms: productive either of good or evil
transmission_notes: The category is the cited Ashmand rendering of Ptolemy's Proclus-based text; 'common influence' is preserved as source terminology rather than mapped to a later sect or benefic technique.
